## gh auth login
Authenticate `gh` with a GitHub account — browser flow, device code, or PAT — and store the credential securely in the system keyring.

## gh auth
Manage GitHub CLI authentication — log in, log out, inspect token scopes, and switch active accounts across multiple GitHub hosts and identities.

## gh auth refresh
Expand, shrink, or reset the OAuth scopes on the active account's stored token — opens a browser re-auth flow to apply the change.

## gh issue create
Open a new GitHub Issue with title, body, labels, assignees, milestone, and project — fully non-interactively from the command line.

## gh issue develop
Create a branch that is server-side linked to a GitHub Issue — making the branch visible in the issue's "Development" panel — and optionally check it out locally in one step.

## gh issue
Create, browse, and manage GitHub Issues from the terminal — the entry point to every issue workflow.

## gh label
Create, list, edit, delete, and clone labels across GitHub repositories.

## gh licenses _(stub)_

## gh org _(stub)_

## gh pr create
Open a new pull request on GitHub from the current (or a specified) branch.

## gh pr merge
Merge (or squash-merge, or rebase-merge) a pull request and optionally delete its branch.

## gh pr
Create, review, and manage GitHub pull requests from the command line.

## gh pr review
Submit an approval, a "request changes" review, or a plain comment review on a pull request — without opening a browser.

## gh preview _(stub)_

## gh project field-list
List all fields defined on a GitHub Projects v2 board, including their types, IDs, and — for single-select fields — the option IDs needed for `item-edit` and GraphQL mutations.

## gh project item-list
List (and optionally filter) the items on a GitHub Projects v2 board, with support for the native Projects filter syntax and JSON output for scripting.

## gh project
Manage GitHub Projects v2 — create, list, view, edit, and drive items and fields from the command line.

## gh release create
Create a new GitHub Release for a tag — auto-generating notes, setting draft/prerelease state, and uploading assets in one command.

## gh release
Create, inspect, edit, and delete GitHub Releases — including tag management, release-note generation, and asset uploads.

## gh repo create
Create a new GitHub repository — interactively, from an existing local directory, or fully non-interactively from flags.

## gh repo edit
Edit repository settings — features, merge strategies, topics, visibility, and more — without opening the GitHub web UI.

## gh repo
Create, clone, fork, view, and manage GitHub repositories from the command line.

## gh ruleset _(stub)_

## gh run
Inspect, watch, and manage GitHub Actions workflow runs from the terminal.

## gh run watch
Stream live step-by-step progress of a workflow run until it completes.

## gh search code
Search within file contents across all of GitHub (or a specific repo/owner) and return matching code snippets with their file paths and URLs.

## gh search
Search across all of GitHub — code, commits, issues, pull requests, and repositories — from the terminal.

## gh variable
Manage GitHub Actions and Dependabot variables — non-encrypted key/value pairs — at the repository, environment, or organization level.

## gh workflow
List, view, enable, disable, and manually trigger GitHub Actions workflows from the command line.

## gh workflow run
Dispatch a `workflow_dispatch` event to manually trigger a GitHub Actions workflow, optionally passing typed inputs and targeting a specific branch or SHA.
